glossary.Peripheral vestibular disorder: A balance problem arising in the inner ear or vestibular nerve, not the brain.
glossary.Vestibular: Relating to the inner-ear balance system.
glossary.Rotational: Spinning; the sensation that you or the room is turning.
glossary.Inner ear: The fluid-filled part of the ear containing the cochlea (hearing) and the balance organs.
glossary.Head trauma: Injury to the head, which can dislodge otoconia.
glossary.Viral illness: An infection caused by a virus, such as a cold or flu.
glossary.Focal neurological deficit: Loss of function in one part of the nervous system, such as weakness of one limb.
glossary.Neck extension: Tilting the head backwards to look up.
glossary.Manoeuvre: A set sequence of positions or movements done for diagnosis or treatment.
glossary.Horizontal nystagmus: Involuntary side-to-side jerking movements of the eyes.
glossary.Red flag: A feature suggesting a serious underlying cause that needs urgent assessment.
glossary.Weakness: Reduced muscle power, a sign of neurological damage.
glossary.Central cause: A cause in the brain, such as the brainstem or cerebellum, rather than the inner ear.
glossary.Cerebellum: The part of the brain at the back that coordinates balance and movement.
glossary.Brainstem: The base of the brain linking it to the spinal cord, containing balance and eye-movement centres.
glossary.Falls: Unintended drops to the ground; a key risk with sudden vertigo, especially in older people.
glossary.Gold standard: The most accurate, definitive test for a diagnosis.
glossary.Clinical diagnosis: A diagnosis made from history and examination without needing tests.
glossary.Nausea: A feeling of wanting to vomit.
glossary.Repositioning manoeuvres: Head-position sequences, such as Epley, that move otoconia back into the utricle.
glossary.Utricular macula: The sensory patch in the utricle where otoconia normally sit, detecting linear movement and gravity.
glossary.Dependent position: The lowest point when lying down, where loose debris settles by gravity.
glossary.Hearing loss: Reduced ability to hear; absent in BPPV.
glossary.Self-limiting: Gets better on its own without treatment.
glossary.Gravity: The downward pull used by the Epley manoeuvre to move otoconia.
